Fig. 1. Noise analysis for 1/100 noise level and 1/2 noise level LDPET images. Noise image is calculated by the difference between FDPET and LDFET.

Fig. 2. The overview of the training network. The model takes a LDPET image as input and predicts the underlying noise. To prevent the loss of negative noise components, standard ReLU activations within the U-Net are replaced with LeakyReLU activation function. During training, the final denoised PET prediction is processed via a LeakyReLU with a shallow slope 0.01 to prevent neuron death. During inference, the model reverts to ReLU activations for the final output to ensure non-negative PET values.

Fig. 5. Qualitative comparison of denoised lower abdomen using different methods for 1/50 noise level and 1/2 noise level LDPET images. The sample is selected from dataset acquired by the University of Bern.

Fig. 7. Qualitative comparison of whole-body PET denoising using different methods at 1/50 (2%) and 1/2 (50%) dose levels. Images are presented as Maximum Intensity Projections (MIP) along the longitudinal (z) axis. The rows display sample cases from the Shanghai Ruijin Hospital dataset. Columns from left to right: LDPET input, outputs from individually trained Unet models, results from the proposed network, and the FDPET ground truth.

Fig. 6. Comparison of denoised lower abdomen using different methods for 1/50 noise level and 1/2 noise level LDPET images. The sample is selected from dataset acquired by the University of Bern. Top row is denoised PET image by UNN and proposed method. Bottom row is the difference between the denoised PET image and FDPET.
